- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.5), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots; cap forecast at +10% above recent peak for 3–5 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive days below 65), model tends to lag; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% per day.
- When sentiment flips from positive to negative, model often fails to adjust quickly; delay forecast correction by 1–2 days.
- If model forecast is > 10% above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward bias of 1–3% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating +/–), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values.
